title: POI Address Queries
description: Rules for evaluating results when the user queries a specific Point of Interest (POI) such as a museum, park, hospital, school, library, theater, or other named place.

decision_logic.condition: Result is the exact POI queried (same name, same location)
decision_logic.notes: Perfect match — user navigates directly to this POI

decision_logic.condition: Result is a different name but is the same physical POI (official vs. colloquial name, or building/complex name)
decision_logic.notes: Same place, different name — still a perfect navigational result

decision_logic.condition: Result is the same category of POI (e.g., another museum) in the same area/neighborhood
decision_logic.notes: Same type of POI, same general area — high relevance

decision_logic.condition: Result is the same category of POI in the same city but different neighborhood
decision_logic.notes: Same type, same city but not exact area

decision_logic.condition: Result is a related but different category of POI (e.g., art gallery for a museum query)
Result is unrelated to the queried POI type or location
decision_logic.notes: No meaningful connection to the POI query

exceptions: Well-known POIs (major landmarks) have stricter Navigational criteria — only the exact POI qualifies
If a POI has multiple entrances or buildings, any official entrance/building rates Navigational
For hospital queries, showing the ER entrance vs. main entrance both rate Navigational

conditions: 'The Met' is the official colloquial name for the Metropolitan Museum of Art
calibration_examples.reasoning: Same POI, official colloquial name — step 2 applies

conditions: Located in same area of Chicago
calibration_examples.reasoning: Same POI category (museum) in same area — step 3 applies

conditions: Bryant Park is in a different neighborhood of NYC
calibration_examples.reasoning: Same category (park), same city but different neighborhood — step 4 applies
No meaningful connection to the museum query — step 6 applies
